title: obdeect versus sim_telarray
reading_guide: **What is compared.** Each case compares obdeect with a reference: an analytic expectation, a sim_telarray, LightEmission or CORSIKA program, or both. Signed values are obdeect / reference − 1, ratios are obdeect / reference, ± is one standard error.

**What PASS means.** All gated checks of the case are inside limits fixed before the run (`details.json`). Where a reference program is known to be wrong, the case is gated against the analytic expectation, and the comparison with that program is *recorded only*: shown, but not part of the verdict.

**Kind of test.** Format: the data arrive unchanged (no physics). Calculation: a deterministic formula, compared point by point. Monte Carlo: random photons or showers are generated and compared as distributions, with statistical errors. Ray tracing: photons are traced through the telescope optics.

**Same frame before comparing.** obdeect light sources write photons where they are emitted, the LightEmission programs where they arrive. Before comparing, obdeect photons are moved to the reference plane (flight time added). The time panels show the arrival times as compared.
**Known features of the reference programs.** Some differences in the plots come from the reference, not from obdeect; each affected case has an *Expected differences* box under its figure.

- ff-1m, ff-gct and fake-muon write times in steps of 1/32 ns: their time histograms show spikes or a comb, obdeect times are continuous. Means and widths are compared. Cause (from the sim_telarray source): the programs write bunches in the CORSIKA IACT long format, where the time is a 32-bit float relative to a time offset (about 4e5 ns for a 20° 'shower' from the top of the atmosphere, `iact.c`, `toffset`); a float between 2¹⁸ and 2¹⁹ ns has a step of 2⁻⁵ ns = 1/32 ns. Not a physics effect, and 31 ps is small against the pulses.

- nsbls samples the photon entry point wrongly (radius `1 − sqrt(u)` instead of `sqrt(u)`, rotated azimuth): its entry-point, time and camera distributions differ from the analytic expectation, which obdeect follows.
- fake-muon times deviate slightly from the analytic distribution; obdeect follows it.

**Image χ²/ndf (chain cases).** Camera images of the same event and telescope from the two runs, pixel by pixel: mean over pixels with signal of (a − b)² / (a + b), with a, b the photoelectrons of the pixel in each run. Differences from Poisson fluctuations alone give about 1; systematic shape differences give more (limit 2). Values below 1 mean the two runs share part of their fluctuations (e.g. identical photons in the stream round trip). For light sources the summed images are compared the same way (χ² per pixel of the normalised images).
**KS.** Largest difference of two cumulative distributions, compared with the critical value for the sample sizes (in brackets where shown).

**Optics.** The star is moved off axis along x (E/W) and along y (N/S). The optics are not rotationally symmetric, so off axis the two directions give different values; each figure shows both, and both programs must agree for each direction.

steps.title: Photon stream format
steps.intro: The obdeect photon stream must carry CORSIKA photons and light-source photons to sim_telarray without loss: CORSIKA → stream → sim_telarray EventIO, compared with sim_telarray on the original CORSIKA file.

steps.title: Atmosphere (propagation)
steps.intro: obdeect propagation (extinction, refraction, travel time) against analytic results, sim_telarray's extinction tables and the compiled CORSIKA atmosphere code.

steps.title: Light sources
steps.intro: obdeect light sources against the sim_telarray LightEmission programs and analytic expectations: photon yield, directions, times and wavelengths at emission, then camera photoelectrons in sim_telarray. Signed values are obdeect / reference − 1; ratios are obdeect / reference.

steps.title: Telescope optics
steps.intro: Ray tracing of obdeect against sim_telarray for the same telescope model, star light at 0–4° off axis along two directions: PSF (D80), effective mirror area and effective focal length.

steps.title: Full chain
steps.intro: obdeect stages inserted into the CORSIKA → sim_telarray chain, compared event by event with the direct sim_telarray run on the same showers and seeds. Bias = obdeect / reference − 1 of camera photoelectrons, with its standard error.

steps.title: Earth curvature (large zenith angles)
steps.intro: At large zenith angles the plane-parallel atmosphere is no longer accurate. obdeect propagation has two curved modes: `spherical` (obdeect applies curvature: emission altitude, extinction and refraction in spherical shells) and `corsika` (CORSIKA with the CURVED option has already curved the shower; obdeect applies the curved extinction only). These cases check the curved geometry and extinction against analytic results and an independent ray tracer, the CURVED flags from CORSIKA through the stream, the mode rules, and CURVED CORSIKA showers at 65° and 75° through obdeect and sim_telarray. sim_telarray itself is plane-parallel, so at these angles it is a reference for the method, not for the result.

steps.title: End-to-end robustness and determinism
steps.intro: Whole-chain properties that do not compare with a reference program: identical output for identical input (threads, chunking, pipes, tee fan-out), rejection of tampered efficiency ledgers, and graceful failure on damaged streams. Pass means zero mismatches and zero silent accepts, with positive controls accepted.

steps.title: Performance: obdeect chain against sim_telarray
steps.intro:
How fast is the obdeect chain on the same showers as sim_telarray, and where does the time go? Report only, apart from a few time budgets (checks below each case).

**What is compared**

Two ways from the same CORSIKA file to camera images:

```
sim_telarray:   CORSIKA file ─▶ sim_telarray [atmosphere + optics + camera]

obdeect chain:  CORSIKA file ─▶ from-corsika ─▶ propagation ─▶ trace-stream ─▶ to-simtel ─▶ sim_telarray [camera only]
                                (read photons)   (atmosphere)   (optics)        (hand over)   (Bypass_Optics=3)
```

The five obdeect programs are connected by a pipe and run at the same time. The camera is the same sim_telarray code on both sides, so the differences come from how the photons reach the camera.

- **QE pre-selection** ("envelope" in the code, "efficiency bound" in obdeect): most Cherenkov photons are never detected, because the quantum efficiency (QE) of the photodetectors is at most about 40 % and much lower at most wavelengths. sim_telarray traces every photon through the optics and drops most of them only in the camera. With QE pre-selection, obdeect's propagation keeps each photon already at the start, with a probability just above the best QE at its wavelength (QE / 0.73); the camera then applies the remaining factor (0.73). The expected signal is unchanged, which each run checks by comparing the camera images (photoelectrons, image shape, arrival times), and about nine of ten photons are dropped before the optics. The saving in computing time is much smaller than that: without pre-selection the photons stay in CORSIKA's bunches of several photons, and trace-stream itself drops most of them just before tracing (by the mirror reflectivity), so the work per shower changes less than the photon count.
- Same showers, same telescope models (CTAO North, production 7.0.0, 20° zenith), same machine. Every obdeect program runs with one thread unless a table says otherwise.

**How to read the times**

- **CPU time** is the processor time summed over all programs: what a batch farm pays. **Wall time** is the elapsed time. In a pipe the five obdeect programs run at the same time on different cores, so the chain's wall time is shorter than its CPU time; on a single core it would be at least the CPU time.
- Ratios are obdeect chain / sim_telarray: below 1 means obdeect is faster.
- Building the optical model (`ray-tracing: compile`, about 0.3 s per run) is left out of the chain times unless stated; it is listed on its own.
- **Timing unreliable** = 1: the machine was busy (load above 1) or the repetitions differ by more than 5 %. Repetitions alternate between sim_telarray and obdeect, so both see the same conditions; the "fastest repetition" ratios use the fastest run of each, closest to an idle machine.

stream.corsika-roundtrip.differences: The photons are not bit-identical: the stream stores positions in m as float32, so x, y and emission height come back with a relative error up to {max_codec_normalized_error:.2f} × 1e-6 (the codec bound); directions, times, wavelengths and bunch sizes are exact. A change this small can still move a photon across a mirror or camera edge in sim_telarray and shift its random-number sequence for the rest of the event, so a few pixels differ (image χ²/ndf {mean_image_reduced_chi2:.2f}, below 1: the runs share most fluctuations). The mean bias ({photoelectron_relative_bias:+.2%} ± {photoelectron_relative_bias_se:.2%}) is zero within errors and no trigger changes. The mechanism is the expected one, not isolated.

stream.direction-roundtrip.title: Full-sphere photon directions: stream round trip and to-simtel rejection
stream.direction-roundtrip.headline: photons {photon_count:.0f}, bit mismatches {bit_mismatch_count}, up / down / horizontal count deltas {cz_upward_count_delta} / {cz_downward_count_delta} / {cz_horizontal_count_delta}, to-simtel refused upward+horizontal in {rejected_cases} of 2 frames, camera accepts any sign {camera_any_sign_accepted} of 1, downward converted {accepted_downward} of 3
stream.direction-roundtrip.description: A grid of 1000 unit vectors over the full sphere (Fibonacci grid with exact vertical and horizontal directions) is written as a format 1.1 `.pst` stream in each frame (sky, ground, telescope, camera), read back, and compared column by column at the bit level. In the ground and telescope frames, which sim_telarray reads with the sign of cz, a stream with one upward and one horizontal photon must be refused by `obdeect stream to-simtel` with the message that sim_telarray does not store the sign of cz. In the camera frame, where only cx and cy are used, a stream with upward, downward and horizontal photons must convert. In every frame a downward-only stream of the same layout must convert. Needs obdeect only.

propagation.upward-lidar.title: Upward laser light: single scattering into an off-axis telescope
propagation.upward-lidar.headline: total yield pulls {up_100m_total_yield_pull:+.1f} / {up_1km_total_yield_pull:+.1f} / {down_100m_total_yield_pull:+.1f} (100 m, 1 km, downward control); time chi2/ndf {up_100m_time_chi2_ndf:.2f} / {up_1km_time_chi2_ndf:.2f} / {down_100m_time_chi2_ndf:.2f}; plane counts off by {up_100m_plane_up_count_error} / {up_1km_plane_up_count_error}
propagation.upward-lidar.description: A laser at 1 m above the observation level (obdeect scatters primaries only above it) fires upwards at 20 deg from the zenith, w = 1 at 355 nm, with the molecular and aerosol table of the scattering cases. Single scattering (obdeect, one primary per call) into a telescope sphere of radius 12.5 m centred 30 m above the observation level, at 100 m and 1 km horizontal distance; scattering points below the centre send light upwards. A vertical downward beam from 48 km above the observation level into the 100 m telescope is the downward control. The reference is the numerical lidar equation written in the adapter with numpy and the documented phase functions (Rayleigh with the table depolarization, Henyey-Greenstein), the transmission table of the telescope path, the aim-point disc average of the documented estimator, and the arrival time (s + D) / c at the sphere centre (no air profile). Gates: total yield pull within 4 standard errors; per-bin chi2/ndf within 3 sigma of one and per-bin pulls within 4; scattered photons sent through the sky to G with extinction off: photons reaching the plane with cz > 0 from below it and cz < 0 from above it, and the photons moving away, exact; empty reference bins receive no photons.

The reference is written from the bytes: the EventIO items are walked here (the sync tag and the 12-byte item headers, containers without sync tags), the 1217 body is decoded here, and each bunch gives its emission point E = A - dist d and the sphere row by the documented rules (entry point, path, time ctime + (s - dist)/c, zem = observation level + telescope z + E_z). Rows are compared in float32 ulp, misses by count. `obdeect stream to-simtel` must refuse the full run (a photon emitted inside the sphere) and convert a subset of downward on-sphere rows, which must land on the plane z = 0 along their lines; the sim_telarray output is read with pyeventio (block 1205).

propagation.sphere-extinction.title: Extinction of sphere rows: plane formula, chord integral (flat and spherical), continuity at |u| = 0.1, plane and sphere rows
propagation.sphere-extinction.headline: steep rows {a_steep_max_rel_error:.1e}, near-horizontal and horizontal chords {b_chord_flat_max_rel_error:.1e} (flat) and {b_chord_spherical_max_rel_error:.1e} (spherical), continuity {c_continuity_max_rel_error:.1e} (formula difference {c_formula_depth_difference:.0e}), plane vs sphere {d_plane_vs_sphere_max_rel:.1e}
propagation.sphere-extinction.description: Sky photons aimed at one telescope (centre 30 m above the observation level, radius 12.5 m; transmission table fixtures/atm_trans_2000_1_10_0_0_2000.dat, H2 = 2000 m, no profile). The run is weighted with store_p, so each row's p is its transmission. Reference, written in the adapter from the table class (log10-linear in height, linear in wavelength, derivative of the same interpolation) and scipy quad: for steep rows (|u| >= 0.1) p = exp(-|tau(h_E) - tau(h_Q)|/|u|) with h_E = zem and h_Q the altitude of the row point; for |u| < 0.1 the chord integral of k = |dtau/dh| from E = Q - L d to Q, flat (h linear) and spherical (Earth radius 6371315 m, centre (0, 0, -(R + H2)), h = |X - centre| - R). Continuity: the two reference forms agree at |u| = 0.1, and rows on both sides of 0.1 agree with their branch. Plane and sphere rows of the same photons, the sphere entry on the equator of the telescope: transmissions agree to 1e-6. Photons emitted inside the sphere have p = 1. Gate: 1e-6 relative (the documented quadrature agreement); the spherical chord is the open point (see the report).

propagation.sphere-geometry.title: Sphere representation of the atmosphere stage: geometry, refraction and determinism
propagation.sphere-geometry.headline: no refraction: {no_refraction_rows} photons, kept and drop reasons equal, budget ratio {no_refraction_budget_ratio_max:.2f}; refraction: hybrid rule {refraction_hybrid_position_m:.1e} m, integrator {refraction_integrator_position_m:.1e} m, turning ray {turning_position_m:.1e} m; determinism mismatches {determinism_mismatch_count}
propagation.sphere-geometry.description: Sky photons in all directions (downward, horizontal, upward from below, emitted inside the sphere, below the observation level, aimed past the sphere) against one telescope of radius 12.5 m at 20 m. Without refraction the references are the straight-line entry points, times and drop reasons, compared with a float32 budget (one spacing plus the direction budget 2 eps s, since the stored direction is unit to 6e-8). With the atmospheric profile the reference integrates the ray equation d(n d)/ds = grad n with scipy (DOP853, rtol 1e-12; the same profile interpolation as the documented one), with a two-phase search so that the sphere chord (about 14 m) is always resolved. Gates: hybrid rows and integrator rows 1e-4 m; times 1e-4 ns plus one float32 spacing; a turning ray (apex about 870 m, path 560 km, sphere centred on its descending crossing) 5e-3 m. Determinism: identical rows for chunk sizes 1 and 7, four threads, and a permuted input order.

sources.ground-muon.description: A 120 m track at 3.6 m impact (1e5 photons, Cherenkov cone 1.2 degrees, beta = 1) and an isotropic point 57 m from the sphere centre (2e5 photons), frame ground, one telescope of radius 12.5 m. Every row is checked against the analytic geometry, with its emission point rebuilt from the row: inside rows are the emission points on the track (path 0); entry points lie on the sphere with path |r - P| and time (s_emit + path)/c; zem is the observation level plus the emission height. Counts: the inside rows of the track are Binomial(N, chord/L), the kept point photons Binomial(N, (1 - sqrt(1 - (R/D)^2))/2), both as pulls; misses_sphere equals the photons emitted minus the rows written.

optics.sphere-vs-plane.title: Ray tracing from the telescope sphere: plane rows and sphere entry rows of the same photons
optics.sphere-vs-plane.headline: segmented fixture: detected sets identical ({fixture_detected_plane} photons), position difference {fixture_max_position_difference_m:.1e} m, time {fixture_max_time_difference_ns:.1e} ns; LST: {lst_detected_set_mismatch} set mismatches, time budget ratio {lst_time_budget_ratio:.2f}; horizontal rows traced {horizontal_rows_traced}; enclosure rejects 0.5 m {enclosure_small_rejected}
optics.sphere-vs-plane.description: A parallel beam from a star at zenith 20 degrees (downward photons, the telescope pointed along the beam) is propagated in plane mode (G rows on the plane through the telescope centre) and in sphere mode (entry rows), and both go through trace-stream with the same optical model. The detected sets must be identical; camera positions and directions must agree within float32 rounding of the rows (budget four spacings, two roundings per path). Times: plane rows are moved to the ground input plane at vacuum speed and their traced path is multiplied by the group index n_g, while sphere rows start at their entry point; the expected difference is (1 - n_g) D / c per photon, D = (P - E) . d along the ray (P: plane row moved to the input plane, E: sphere entry). The residual after this convention is gated on float32 rounding; the raw difference is reported with its size (LST: up to 6.8e-3 ns, the convention explains 6.2e-3 ns, n_g = 1.000226). The segmented fixture is always compared; LSTN-01 when the simulation models are present (VALIDATION_MODELS or /models). Horizontal sphere rows of the tilted fixture telescope are traced without rejection, and the enclosure check rejects a 0.5 m sphere and accepts the fixture sphere of 9 m (camera front 8.52 m from the centre).
